title: California just cause eviction requirement (Tenant Protection Act)
requirement: An owner may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice once a tenant has occupied 12 months; no-fault terminations require one month's rent as relocation assistance or a rent waiver.
key_value: Just cause after 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
coverage_conditions: Residential real property after 12 months' continuous occupancy (24 months if new adult tenants added), except housing certified within 15 years, owner-occupied homes up to two units, non-corporate owners of separate-title property, and deed-restricted affordable housing.

conditions.who: owner not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member

conditions.text: deed- or agreement-restricted affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income

applicability.per_tenancy: Just cause applies only after all tenants have continuously occupied 12 months, or one tenant 24 months; excludes a tenancy sharing bathroom or kitchen with the owner.
coverage_quotes: (7) Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.
(A) A residence in which the owner-occupant rents or leases no more than two units or bedrooms, including, but not limited to, an accessory dwelling unit or a junior accessory dwelling unit.

(9) Housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction contained in an agreement with a government agency, or other recorded document as affordable housing for persons and families of very low, low, or moderate income, as defined in Section 50093 of the Health and Safety Code

exemptions: Transient hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and residential-care facilities; dormitories; units sharing bathroom or kitchen with owner; owner-occupied single-family residences up to two units; owner-occupied duplexes; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; alienable separate property with non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
penalty: A noncompliant termination notice is void; the owner is liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages for willful acts, and the Attorney General or local counsel may seek injunctive relief.
quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
interaction: Local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or more protective ones, govern instead of this section.

relations.quote: (A) Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.
(2) A residential real property shall not be subject to both a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy and this section.
